title: Input length counting loop
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with oracle, and let $r$ be a register and $j$ an oracle index. Suppose state `scan` calls oracle $j$ on the whole input and the single register $r$, proceeding to `inc` on a positive answer and `done` otherwise; state `inc` increments $r$ and returns to `scan`. Suppose that for every $n\le |x|$, the oracle answers positively on the encoding of $x$ paired with the binary word of $n$ exactly when $n<|x|$. If $|x|\le B$, all initial registers are at most $B$, and the initial value of $r$ is at most $|x|$, then the program reaches `done` with $r=|x|$, while every configuration before that endpoint satisfies $\mathrm{PreS}$ and keeps all registers at most $B$.
